newsitem.title: UK: JERSEY SAYS COLLECTIVE FUNDS TOP 35 BILLION STG.
newsitem.headline: JERSEY SAYS COLLECTIVE FUNDS TOP 35 BILLION STG.

text.p: Funds under management in Jersey's investment industry rose by more than 1.9 billion sterling to a record 35.2 billion sterling in the second quarter of 1997, Jersey's financial services department said on Tuesday.

"We have broken the record for funds under management in siX out of the past eight quarters. Over the past year, funds under management are up by 7.2 billion sterling which is over 25 percent," said Martin Dryden, chairman of the Jersey Fund Managers Association.

The total number of funds fell to 324 from 332 and sub-funds and investment pools drooped to 1014 from 1017. The decrease is partly attributable to a trend toward umbrella funds at the expense of single-class funds, the financial services department said.
Bond and fixed-interest funds rose by 21 percent to 2.4 billion sterling.
Japanese equity funds rose by 38 percent to 1.4 billion sterling.
